permissionModes.source: the ceiling of MRC2-03-01: permissionVocabularyOf() reads each provider definition (fullAccessArgs / yoloModeArgs, readOnlyArgs, readOnlyCliEnforced); managedPermissionModeProblem() measures a requested mode against the pin by width (readonly < standard < full); managedArgsProblems() refuses by name every full-access flag and every mode flag whose value names full access under a pin below full, and under readonly refuses a provider that cannot enforce read-only on its command line and a command line that does not carry its read-only flags; buildAgentArgs() under managedCeiling throws the same mode problem before any flag is emitted. Nothing is lowered to fit.
permissionModes.method: for every defined provider but the internal terminal, the real batch argument set of each requested mode (buildAgentArgs with the definition, its base args, a prompt and permissionMode) was measured under a ceiling pinning none, readonly, standard and full: the mode check first, then the flag check on the resulting arguments; commandLineReads is what cliRequestedPermissionMode() reads back off that command line (what a CLI or headless surface would hand the plan)

verdicts.admitted: the request fits the pin and its arguments carry nothing the pin forbids
verdicts.refused-by-mode: the requested mode is wider than the pin (the one width rule); refused before any flag is looked at
verdicts.refused-by-flag: the mode fits but the arguments the provider would run with carry a flag the pin forbids, or (readonly) the read-only flags are missing or unenforceable; refused by name, never rewritten

readOnly.enforced: readOnlyCliEnforced: true with read-only flags: the command line enforces the mode and a readonly pin demands exactly those flags
readOnly.enforced-by-default: readOnlyCliEnforced: true with no flag (Factory Droid exec is read-only unless widened): a readonly pin is satisfied by the absence of a widening flag
readOnly.accepted: readOnlyCliEnforced: false with a flag the provider accepts but does not enforce (prompt-only): a readonly pin refuses the provider by name rather than trusting the flag
readOnly.none: no read-only flag and no enforcement: a readonly pin refuses the provider

fullAccess.flag: full access is asked for with a flag on the command line, which the ceiling measures (managedArgsProblems) and which cliRequestedPermissionMode reads back as full
fullAccess.env-only: full access is an environment setting (OpenCode OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT with "*": "allow", set by the definition in every mode but read-only through readOnlyEnvOverrides) that no argument check sees; held at the request level only (the mode a surface names), and the standard arguments run with it
fullAccess.flagless: the provider has no full-access flag: a full request leaves the standard arguments, is read back as standard, and is held at the request level only

standardRequestRefusedUnderStandardPin.reason: batchModeArgs carry a full-access flag, so the standard (headless) argument set itself asks for full access; the ceiling measures the flag, not the mode label, and the command line reads back as full. Only a readonly request of these providers fits under a standard pin. Closing it means a standard batch argument set without the bypass per provider (a definition change that alters the unmanaged default), recorded at MRC2-03-03A and not made in P2-03

readonlyRequestRefusedUnderReadonlyPin.reason: gemini-cli: its read-only arguments are -y, a full-access flag, refused by name; antigravity: --sandbox is accepted but not enforced (readOnlyCliEnforced: false); hermes: no read-only flag and no enforcement. A readonly pin refuses these providers rather than trusting a label

fullRequestLeavesNoFlag.reason: no full-access flag (pi, omp) or an environment setting (opencode): a full request is held at the request level (buildAgentArgs under managedCeiling, the launch plan, the desktop handler) and never on the command line; a CLI surface reads it back as standard

envOnlyFullAccess.reason: OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT is not a route-controlling name the environment ceiling strips, so a standard OpenCode turn under a standard pin runs with the definition's blanket allow; the ceiling holds the named mode, not the effect

src/main/codex-app-server/invocation.ts codexSandboxCeiling: readonly -> read-only, standard -> workspace-write, full or none -> unpinned; a wider sandbox refused at the app-server sink, never the exec fallback (MRC2-03-03, 03-03A)

src/main/agents/provider-probe.ts: a probe's own arguments under the route ceiling (boundUtilityRoute), the slash probe's --dangerously-skip-permissions refused under standard or readonly (MRC2-03-04, 04A)

src/shared/maestro-lib/managed/tui-handshake.ts + src/maestro-p: the handshake carries the ceiling's permissionMode; checkTuiSpawn refuses a bypass above it before pty.spawn and withPermissionBypass withholds it (MRC2-03-05, 05A, 06)
permissionModes.producer: none in this build: ProcessSpawnAuthorityPort.routeCeiling / permissionCeiling (desktop) and HeadlessSpawnAuthority.routeCeiling (CLI, plugins) have no production producer (CP-01); every verdict in this section is the consumer's answer to a ceiling a test port lends, proven by permission-ceiling.test.ts, agent-args.managed.test.ts, handle-spawn.managed.test.ts, agent-spawner.test.ts and invocation.test.ts
permissionModes.routeReconciliation: providerRouteSupport() reports managed: implemented on child-process only (the launch admitted at the real spawn) and unsupported on pty, codex-app-server, opencode-server and ssh; P2-03 adds ceiling CONSUMERS at the codex-app-server sink (sandbox) and the local pty the maestro-p TUI uses for claude-code (handshake), but no enforcement producer, so the route words stand unchanged; a managed route on an SSH remote is refused by the plan
